title: Brahma Sutra Bhashya of Ramanuja
altTitles: Vedanta-Sutras with the Commentary of Ramanuja
author: ramanuja
attributionNote: Composed by Ramanuja, the principal theologian of the Sri Vaishnava school, as a commentary on Badarayana's Brahma Sutras. It is a distinct work from Shankara's commentary on the same sutras, and the two are kept as separate records.
description: Ramanuja's commentary on the Brahma Sutras, the foundational statement of Vishishtadvaita Vedanta: Brahman is the supreme person, the world and souls are its real modes, and liberation is attained through devotion and the Lord's grace. Thibaut's translation prints the sutras with the full commentary, in four adhyayas of four padas each.
historicalContext: The Sri Bhashya belongs to the Sri Vaishnava commentarial tradition of the eleventh and twelfth centuries. George Thibaut translated it for the Sacred Books of the East (volume 48, 1904), the standard public-domain English rendering.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Project Gutenberg at read time. All four adhyayas and sixteen padas are present in this edition; the passage index follows the pada divisions of Thibaut's translation.
